headline: Low pairwise risk overall; no shared filesystem or network path, but OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/API surfaces create a limited prompt-injection and cascading-error pathway if its outputs are manually bridged into whisper workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and APIs, while whisper has no MCP, clipboard, or screen-capture surface. That makes an automatic injection bridge unlikely, but manual copy-paste or file handoff could still carry malicious instructions from OpenBBTerminal into whisper-related prompts or transcripts. The pathway is limited and not default.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal output is manually pasted into a prompt or transcript consumed by whisper-related tooling, injection becomes plausible.
IF an external orchestrator forwards OpenBBTerminal text into whisper without sanitization, the risk increases.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste bridging between the two tools during review.
Strip instructions from OpenBBTerminal outputs before forwarding them.
Use a fixed template for any text passed into whisper workflows.
Keep whisper isolated from any MCP-fed text streams.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to forwarded content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, but its network egress is none and whisper only handles audio files locally. There is no shared filesystem or authenticated cloud principal shown, so direct leakage between them is not evidenced. Residual risk is limited to operator-mediated transfer of sensitive financial content into audio workflows.
conditions: IF the operator exports OpenBBTerminal financial outputs into audio files processed by whisper, sensitive data can cross domains.
IF a shared workspace is introduced outside the profiles, leakage risk rises.
mitigations: Avoid placing financial exports into shared folders.
Redact sensitive fields before any audio conversion.
Use separate directories for each agent.
Confirm whisper jobs only read intended audio files.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, or use network egress, so there is no overlapping mutable resource to contend over. OpenBBTerminal supports multiple instances, and whisper does not expose write or coordination capabilities. The pairwise conflict pathway is therefore blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory, conflict risk would need reassessment.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, the current none rating no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Do not mount a shared writable workspace.
Avoid shared git repositories.
Recheck permissions after any deployment change.
requires-engineering: add lock-based coordination if writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can emit financial analysis through APIs/MCP, and whisper can produce transcripts or downstream text that an operator may treat as authoritative. There is no documented verification step between them, so if OpenBBTerminal output is forwarded into whisper-based workflows, errors can cascade into multiple work products. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal outputs are used as inputs to whisper-driven transcription or summarization, unverified errors can propagate.
IF an operator relies on whisper output without cross-checking against source data, cascading error becomes more likely.
mitigations: Require human review of OpenBBTerminal outputs before reuse.
Compare any derived text against source financial data.
Label forwarded content as unverified.
Use a second independent check for high-stakes outputs.
requires-engineering: add automated validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while whisper touches audio and speech. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles, so only a limited compliance concern remains: if regulated financial data is converted into audio or transcripts, policy handling may diverge. The other agent is cited because the risk is about cross-domain handling.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is converted into audio or transcript artifacts, retention and access policies must be rechecked.
IF the deployment adds jurisdiction-specific data handling rules, compliance scope changes.
mitigations: Classify any derived audio/transcripts before storage.
Avoid embedding sensitive financial data in speech artifacts.
Review retention settings for both workflows.
Keep secrets out of shared outputs.
requires-engineering: document jurisdiction and retention policy mapping.
